Communication dated 12.2.1935 from the Persian Consulate-General 
rei s. H, Yabroff. 


Enquiries show that Solomon Girshevitoh Yabroff (Jabroff ) 
is a Russian Jew who wae born on March 15, 1872 at Hogaisk, 
South Russia. He arrived in Shanghai from Harbin on 
May 15, 1933 and on June 22 of the same year registered with 
the Public Safety Bureau as a Persian subject on the strength 
of Chinese passport No. 824 issued at Hurbin. On August 4, 
1934, he applied to the Public Safety Bureau for registration 
as a person "without nationality" stating that his Persian 
passport had expired and that consequently, he could not be 
registered with the Persian Consulate-General. in Shanghai 
(Copy of application attached). 

Following his arrival in Shanghai Yabroff established a 
law office at House 1, Harmony Terrace, No. 925 Avenue Joffre 
in partnership with a Chinese lawyer named Yuan Shin Yueh 
whe, it is reported, was connected with Soviet circles while 
in Harbin. They act as legal advisors to the local branch 
of the Moscow Narodny Bank (formerly Dalbank) and occasionally 
assisted in the liquidation of warious goods belonging to 
that bank. 

Yabroff is an active member of the local Jewish Zionist 
Revisionist Organization and is the editor of the “Jewish 
Call", a bilingual magazine published by the above organisa~ 
tion in conjunction with another Jewish organization known 
under the name of "Berith Trumpeldore.* § In November 1934, 
in connection with the appearance in the “Jewish Call" of 
an article containing sourrilous attack on the Homanoff 
Imperial family, (File D. 6298) Yabroff's name was mentioned 
in several anomymous handbills among the names of persons 
directly responsible for publishing the article in question. 


-2- . 
The handbills also denounced Yabroff as a Soviet Agent and 
@ person of a doubtful reputation. However, in the Jenuay 
issue of the "Jewish Call" 1% <=° stated that he uad been 
absent to Tientsin at the time when the offending article 
was published and, therefore, could not be held responsible 
for its appearance. 

Yabroff is a widower. His daughter, Mrs. Volsky, 
resides at present in Harbin, while his son, Elias S. Yabroff, 
a naturalised American, resides in Shanghai and is at present 
employed as a shop assistant with the“FPoland Provision Store", 
No. 324 Avenue du Roi Albert. 

Prior to his coming te Shanghai S.H. Yabroff is 
reported t» have been residing for about thirty years in 
Harbin where he was engaged in commercial pursuits and had 
the reputation of being a well-to-do person. In 1919-1921 
he resided at Kobe, Japan, and during that period visited the 
United States. He also made a trip to Europe in 1927/8. 

His business in Harbin is reported to have been unsuccessful 
during the past few years, so that he is believed to have 
incurred considerable debts. It is also rumoured that whihe 


in Harbin he had many friends in Soviet circles and that he had 
business connections with a lawyer named Alexandroff, who is 


a person of doubtful reputation. 
At present he resides at House 1, Harmony Terrace, No. 
925 Avenue Joffre, while his office is situated at No. 225 
Nanking Road (Continental Exporium Building), Rooms 422/35. 
While in Shanghai Yabroff did not come to the notice 
of the Municipal Police in connection with any activities ef

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Section 2, Special Branch.
REPORT
File No.
No. D. 9444.
Date May 15, 1934.

Subject (in full) Solomon G. Yabroff, Soviet Employee.

Made by D.S. Tcheremshansky Forwarded by [Signature] D. S.

Solomon G. Yabroff is a legal advisor to the Far Eastern
Bank (Dalbank). He is a Persian subject of Russian-Jewish
origin, born on March 15, 1872, at Nogaysk. Yabroff arrived
at Shanghai from Harbin in 1933 and registered with the local
Public Safety Bureau on June 2, 1933, under No. 10726 on the
strength of the Chinese Passport No. 6824 issued at Harbin.
Yabroff has a law office at No. 925 Avenue Joffre, house 1,
Harmony Terrace, in partnership with one Boris Nikolaevitch
Uan Sing Un, a Chinese lawyer educated in Russia and formerly
legal advisor to the C.E.R. at Harbin, who was connected with
Soviet circles at Harbin. Yabroff resides at No. 925 Avenue
Joffre, house 1, Harmony Terrace.

[Signature]
D. S.

Officer i/c Special Branch.

主题（全称）所罗门·G·亚布罗夫（Solomon G. Yabroff），苏联雇员。

由 D.S. 切列姆尚斯基（Tcheremshansky）撰写 转呈人 [签名] D. S.

所罗门·G·亚布罗夫是远东银行（Dalbank，即达利银行）的法律顾问。他是波斯籍臣民，具有俄裔犹太人血统，1872年3月15日出生于诺盖斯克（Nogaysk）。亚布罗夫于1933年从哈尔滨抵达上海，并凭在哈尔滨签发的中国护照第6824号，于1933年6月2日在当地公安局登记，登记号为10726。亚布罗夫在霞飞路925号和谐里1号设有一间律师事务所，合伙人为一名叫鲍里斯·尼古拉耶维奇·万星恩（Boris Nikolaevitch Uan Sing Un，音译）的中国律师，该律师曾在俄罗斯受教育，曾任哈尔滨中东铁路（C.E.R.）的法律顾问，并与哈尔滨的苏维埃圈子有联系。亚布罗夫居住在霞飞路925号和谐里1号。

[签名]
D. S.

特务科主管警官
[签名] 15/5

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Section 2, Special Branch
REPORT
Date. Feb. 22, 1935.
Subject. Communication dated 12.2.1935 from the Persian Consulate-General
re: S. H. Yabroff.
Made by D.S. Tcheremshansky Forwarded by.
Enquiries show that Solomon Girshevitch Yabroff (Jabroff)
is a Russian Jew who was born on March 15, 1872 at Nogaisk,
South Russia. He arrived in Shanghai from Harbin on
May 15, 1933 and on June 22 of the same year registered with
the Public Safety Bureau as a Persian subject on the strength
of Chinese passport No. 824 issued at Harbin. On August 4,
1934, he applied at the Public Safety Bureau for registration
as a person "without nationality" stating that his Persian
passport had expired and that consequently, he could not be
registered with the Persian Consulate-General in Shanghai
(Copy of application attached).
Following his arrival in Shanghai Yabroff established a
law office at House 1, Harmony Terrace, No. 925 Avenue Joffre
in partnership with a Chinese lawyer named Yuan Shin Yueh
(who, it is reported, was connected with Soviet circles while
in Harbin.) They act as legal advisors to the local branch
of the Moscow Narodny Bank (formerly Dalbank) and occasionally
assisted in the liquidation of various goods belonging to
that bank.
Yabroff is an active member of the local Jewish Zionist
Revisionist Organization and is the editor of the "Jewish
Call", a bilingual magazine published by the above organiza-
tion in conjunction with another Jewish organization known
under the name of "BRITH Trumpeldore." In November 1934,
in connection with the appearance in the "Jewish Call" of
an article containing scurrilous attack on the Romanoff
Imperial family, (File D. 6298) Yabroff's name was mentioned
in several anonymous handbills among the names of persons
directly responsible for publishing the article in question.

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
特务科第二股
报告
日期：1935年2月22日。
主题：波斯总领事馆1935年2月12日来函，关于 S. H. 亚布罗夫。
由 D.S. 切列姆尚斯基（Tcheremshansky）撰写 转呈人。

经查，所罗门·吉尔舍维奇·亚布罗夫（Jabroff）是一名俄国犹太人，1872年3月15日出生于南俄罗斯的诺盖斯克（Nogaisk）。他于1933年5月15日从哈尔滨抵达上海，并于同年6月22日凭在哈尔滨签发的中国护照第824号，在公安局以波斯籍臣民身份登记。1934年8月4日，他向公安局申请登记为“无国籍”人士，称其波斯护照已过期，因此无法在上海波斯总领事馆登记（附申请书副本）。

亚布罗夫抵沪后，在霞飞路925号和谐里1号与一名叫袁申岳（Yuan Shin Yueh，音译）的中国律师合伙开设了一家律师事务所（据报，袁申岳在哈尔滨期间曾与苏维埃圈子有联系）。他们担任莫斯科国民银行（Moscow Narodny Bank，前身为达利银行）上海分行的法律顾问，并偶尔协助清算该银行所属的各种货物。

亚布罗夫是当地犹太复国主义修正派组织（Jewish Zionist Revisionist Organization）的活跃成员，并担任《犹太呼声》（"Jewish Call"）的编辑，这是一本由上述组织与另一个名为“布里特·特朗普尔多雷”（BRITH Trumpeldore，音译）的犹太组织联合出版的双语杂志。1934年11月，因《犹太呼声》刊登了一篇包含对罗曼诺夫皇室进行恶毒攻击的文章（档案 D. 6298），亚布罗夫的名字出现在几份匿名传单中，被列为直接负责发表该文章的人员之一。

（右上角印章及手写内容：上海公共租界工部局警务处 特务科登记处。档案号 D...）
（左上角小字：I.M. 2 40 1100.1.35）
（右侧手写批注：S.B.Rm Div.）

issue of the "Jewish Call" it was stated that he had been
absent at Tientsin at the time when the offending article
was published and, therefore, could not be held responsible
for its appearance.

Yabroff is a widower. His daughter, Mrs. Volsky,
resides at present in Harbin, while his son, Elias S. Yabroff,
a naturalised American, resides in Shanghai and is at present
employed as a shop assistant with the "Poland Provision Store",
No. 314 Avenue du Roi Albert.

Prior to his coming to Shanghai S.H. Yabroff is
reported to have been residing for about thirty years in
Harbin where he was engaged in commercial pursuits and had
the reputation of being a well-to-do person. In 1919-1921
he resided at Kobe, Japan, and during that period visited the
United States. He also made a trip to Europe in 1927/8.

His business in Harbin is reported to have been unsuccessful
during the past few years, so that he is believed to have
incurred considerable debts. It is also rumoured that while
in Harbin he had many friends in Soviet circles and that he had

a person of doubtful reputation.

At present he resides at House 1, Harmony Terrace, No.
925 Avenue Joffre, while his office is situated at No. 225

While in Shanghai Yabroff did not come to the notice
of the Municipal Police in connection with any activities of

这些传单还谴责亚布罗夫是苏联特工，且名声可疑。然而，《犹太呼声》1月刊指出，在该冒犯性文章发表时，他正不在上海而在天津，因此不应对该文章的发表承担责任。

亚布罗夫是鳏夫。他的女儿沃尔斯基夫人（Mrs. Volsky）目前居住在哈尔滨，而他的儿子伊莱亚斯·S·亚布罗夫（Elias S. Yabroff）已归化美国籍，居住在上海，目前在阿尔贝国王路314号“波兰食品店”（Poland Provision Store）担任店员。

据报，S.H. 亚布罗夫在来上海之前，已在哈尔滨居住约三十年，从事商业活动，并以富裕著称。1919年至1921年间，他居住在日本神户，在此期间曾访问美国。他还于1927/28年前往欧洲旅行。

据报，他在哈尔滨的生意在过去几年中并不成功，因此被认为欠下了巨额债务。另有谣言称，他在哈尔滨期间在苏维埃圈子里有许多朋友，并与一名叫亚历山德罗夫（Alexandroff，音译）的律师有业务往来，此人名声可疑。

目前他居住在霞飞路925号和谐里1号，而其办公室位于南京路225号（大陆商场大楼）422/3室。

亚布罗夫在上海期间，并未因任何不良性质的活动引起工部局警务处的注意。

Section 2, Special Branch XXX
Feb. 22, 35.
Communication dated 12.2.1935 from the Persian Consulate-General
re: S. H. Yabroff.

Enquiries show that Solomon Girshevitch Yabroff (Jabroff)
is a Russian Jew who was born on March 15, 1872 at Nogaisk,
South Russia. He arrived in Shanghai from Harbin on
May 15, 1933 and on June 22 of the same year registered with
the Public Safety Bureau as a Persian subject on the strength
of Chinese passport No. 824 issued at Harbin. On August 4,
1934, he applied to the Public Safety Bureau for registration
as a person "without nationality" stating that his Persian
passport had expired and that consequently, he could not be
registered with the Persian Consulate-General in Shanghai
(Copy of application attached).

Following his arrival in Shanghai Yabroff established a
law office at House 1, Harmony Terrace, No. 925 Avenue Joffre
in partnership with a Chinese lawyer named Yuan Shin Yueh
who, it is reported, was connected with Soviet circles while
in Harbin. They act as legal advisors to the local branch
of the Moscow Narodny Bank (formerly Dalbank) and occasionally
assisted in the liquidation of various goods belonging to
that bank.

Yabroff is an active member of the local Jewish Zionist
Revisionist Organization and is the editor of the "Jewish
Call", a bilingual magazine published by the above organiza-
tion in conjunction with another Jewish organization known
under the name of "Berith Trumpeldore." In November 1934,
in connection with the appearance in the "Jewish Call" of
an article containing scurrilous attack on the Romanoff
Imperial family, (File D. 6298) Yabroff's name was mentioned
in several anonymous handbills among the names of persons
directly responsible for publishing the article in question.
pages.zh:
特务科第二股 XXX
35年2月22日。
波斯总领事馆1935年2月12日来函，关于 S. H. 亚布罗夫。

经查，所罗门·吉尔舍维奇·亚布罗夫（Jabroff）是一名俄国犹太人，1872年3月15日出生于南俄罗斯的诺盖斯克（Nogaisk）。他于1933年5月15日从哈尔滨抵达上海，并于同年6月22日凭在哈尔滨签发的中国护照第824号，在公安局以波斯籍臣民身份登记。1934年8月4日，他向公安局申请登记为“无国籍”人士，称其波斯护照已过期，因此无法在上海波斯总领事馆登记（附申请书副本）。

亚布罗夫抵沪后，在霞飞路925号和谐里1号与一名叫袁申岳（Yuan Shin Yueh，音译）的中国律师合伙开设了一家律师事务所，据报该律师在哈尔滨期间曾与苏维埃圈子有联系。他们担任莫斯科国民银行（前身为达利银行）上海分行的法律顾问，并偶尔协助清算该银行所属的各种货物。

亚布罗夫是当地犹太复国主义修正派组织的活跃成员，并担任《犹太呼声》的编辑，这是一本由上述组织与另一个名为“Berith Trumpeldore”（音译）的犹太组织联合出版的双语杂志。1934年11月，因《犹太呼声》刊登了一篇包含对罗曼诺夫皇室进行恶毒攻击的文章（档案 D. 6298），亚布罗夫的名字出现在几份匿名传单中，被列为直接负责发表该文章的人员之一。

pages.en:
-2-

The handbills also denounced Yabroff as a Soviet Agent and
a person of a doubtful reputation. However, in the January
issue of the "Jewish Call" it was stated that he had been
absent to Tientsin at the time when the offending article
was published and, therefore, could not be held responsible
for its appearance.

Yabroff is a widower. His daughter, Mrs. Volsky,
resides at present in Harbin, while his son, Elias S. Yabroff,
a naturalised American, resides in Shanghai and is at present
employed as a shop assistant with the "Poland Provision Store",
No. 314 Avenue du Roi Albert.

Prior to his coming to Shanghai S.H. Yabroff is
reported to have been residing for about thirty years in
Harbin where he was engaged in commercial pursuits and had
the reputation of being a well-to-do person. In 1919-1921
he resided at Kobe, Japan, and during that period visited the
United States. He also made a trip to Europe in 1927/8.
His business in Harbin is reported to have been unsuccessful
during the past few years, so that he is believed to have
incurred considerable debts. It is also rumoured that while
in Harbin he had many friends in Soviet circles and that he had
business connections with a lawyer named Alexandroff, who is
a person of doubtful reputation.

At present he resides at House 1, Harmony Terrace, No.
925 Avenue Joffre, while his office is situated at No. 225
Nanking Road (Continental Emporium Building), Rooms 422/3.

While in Shanghai Yabroff did not come to the notice
of the Municipal Police in connection with any activities of
an undesirable character.

Jabroff (same name)

Dear Sir,

A certain Salomon Hirchev Jabroff, residing
at No. 2 Harmony Terrace, Avenue Joffre (declaring
himself a Barrister-at-law), has demanded Persian Re-
gistration and has handed me a Passport on which I
have not yet concluded my examination. I shall be
very much obliged for your kindly helping me by in-
forming me of all that is necessary concerning the
said person, and I profit of this occasion to inform
you that according to regulations in Persian Law, all
Persian subjects in China are obliged to register
themselves every year at my Consulate. As my Consu-
late is the only representative of the Imperial Go-
vernment in China, and as you are aware, the new or-
ganisation is in its first year here, for first re-
gistrations I am obliged to make a thorough enquiry
into the documents presented by each declared Persian
subject. Happily, up to the present, I have not had
cause for deeper investigation into the registrations
of Persians residing in Shanghai. This is the only
instance which has drawn my attention, especially since
the passport in question lacks the official stamp and
up to the present I have not been able to read the sig-
nature of the Passport Officer, affixed thereon.

Allow me to thank you in advance,

Yours faithfully,
Key Ostovane
From Key Ostovan, I. P. C.

亲爱的先生，

有一位名叫萨洛蒙·希尔切夫·亚布罗夫（Salomon Hirchev Jabroff）的人，居住在霞飞路和谐里2号（自称是出庭律师），要求办理波斯登记，并向本人提交了一本护照，我尚未完成对该护照的审查。如蒙告知关于该人所需的一切情况，本人将不胜感激。借此机会，我也通知您，根据波斯法律规定，所有在华波斯臣民每年必须在我的领事馆登记。由于我的领事馆是帝国政府在中国的唯一代表，且如您所知，新机构在此处于第一年运作阶段，对于首次登记，我必须对每位自称波斯臣民者提交的文件进行彻底调查。幸运的是，到目前为止，我尚无理由对居住在上海的波斯人的登记进行深入调查。这是唯一引起我注意的案例，特别是因为所涉护照缺少官方印章，且到目前为止，我未能辨认出上面签署的护照官员的签名。

谨此预先致谢，

您忠实的，
凯·奥斯托瓦内（Key Ostovane）
来自凯·奥斯托万（Key Ostovan），伊朗警察总监（I. P. C.）
